The main takeaway from our work is that
X-ray spectra of obscured AGN, even when they are of low quality and have a low signal-to-noise ratio, can be used to estimate the redshift of the source with a precision of ≈0.1.
X-ray spectra, even with low count statistics, can be a useful tool to derive redshifts for obscured AGN, which are otherwise challenging to identify.
, when X-ray redshift estimates are available for obscured AGN, the redshift uncertainties are significantly smaller than those obtained by using only photometric or spectroscopic data.
